wording: Does your company have a written environmental policy that applies to your own operations?
Do you collect and review data on the quality of your sustainability-related information (e.g. checking accuracy of environmental data)?
Does your company have a formal grievance or whistleblower mechanism that employees or stakeholders can use to report concerns?
Does your company publish a sustainability or ESG report (even informally, such as a summary for clients or stakeholders)?
Has your company set a target to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions?
Does your company use due diligence to identify negative sustainability impacts in your supply chain or operations?
Does your company engage with your suppliers on environmental issues (e.g. energy, waste, emissions)?
Do you maintain documentation or records of how your environmental data (e.g. emissions, energy) is compiled and checked?
Does your company have a code of conduct or social-responsibility standards that you expect your suppliers to follow?
Has your company made a public commitment to fight corruption and bribery in all your business activities?
Does your environmental policy address how your products or services affect customers or distributors (downstream impacts)?
Does your company have a plan to transition its business model to be more low-carbon or sustainable?
Does your company consider environmental criteria when selecting or evaluating suppliers?
Has your company set specific, measurable sustainability targets?
Does your company have a written policy that covers labour rights and fair working conditions for all employees?
Has your company assessed which climate-related risks (e.g. extreme weather, rising costs) could affect its business?

Does your company measure or estimate greenhouse-gas emissions that come directly from your own operations  -  for example from company vehicles, boilers, or on-site processes (sometimes called Scope 1 emissions)?
Does your company measure or estimate greenhouse-gas emissions from the electricity or heat it purchases from external suppliers (sometimes called Scope 2 emissions)?
Does your company track its total energy consumption?
Have you identified which of your suppliers face significant actual or potential negative environmental impacts?
Does your company have a plan to reduce the use of non-renewable or hazardous materials in its products or processes?
Does your company track the total volume of water it uses or withdraws?
Does your company track the total amount of waste it generates?
Does your company run or support a formal community investment, philanthropy, or local-impact programme?
Does your company support women-owned businesses or promote inclusive procurement in its supplier relationships?
Does your company assess the quality of activity data and emission factors used for GHG reporting?
Does your company monitor air pollution emissions from your operations - such as smoke, dust, nitrogen oxides, or other particulates?
Does your company generate revenue from remanufactured products or remanufacturing services?
For products such as diesel engines or industrial equipment, do you publish NOx and particulate-matter performance data?
Does your company operate take-back programmes to collect end-of-life products for remanufacturing or recycling?
Are your Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions verified by an independent third party?
Does your company disclose the total number of directors on your board?
Does your company have a Whistleblowing Policy to protect employees who report concerns?
Does your company publish a sustainability or ESG report aligned with a recognised framework (e.g. GRI, ISSB, SASB)?
Does your company disclose the nature of its business operations and principal sustainability-related activities in a publicly available report?
Does your company track progress against sustainability plans or commitments you have previously disclosed?
Do you actively track and report progress against your sustainability targets? (If you don't have targets, leave blank)
Does your company record child-labour or forced-labour incidents identified in your operations or supply chain?
Does your company disclose its spending on sustainability-related research, innovation, or product improvements?
